definition: Automated journalism, also known as algorithmic journalism or robot journalism, describes modern technological processes that are now in use in the journalistic profession, such as news articles and videos generated by computer programs.
details: There are four main fields of application for automated journalism, namely automated content production, data mining, news dissemination and content optimization. Through generative AI, stories are produced automatically by computers rather than human reporters. In the 2020s, generative pre-trained transformers have enabled the generation and summarization of large amounts of information at scale. Increasingly, artificial intelligence (AI) is being used to optimize workflows across newsrooms, including drafting, editing, summarization, research and content optimization. Recent research has focused on expanding the topic of automated journalism to include AI-assisted newsroom workflows that go beyond the idea of content creation. While automated journalism is seen by advocates as efficient and an opportunity to free journalists from routine reporting in sectors including finance, sports, and election coverage, critics raise concerns about what its use means for transparency, accountability, employment and editorial responsibility in the profession. As AI-assisted systems integrate further into newsroom operations, scholars are focused on how their use will impact journalistic ethics

explainer.lead: Automated journalism uses computer programs to help produce and distribute news, from turning data into articles to summarizing and editing text. It can take routine work off journalists’ plates, but it also raises questions about transparency, accountability, jobs, and editorial responsibility.

tiers.eli5: It is like giving a newsroom a very fast kitchen helper: you provide ingredients such as sports scores or election figures, and it helps prepare the story. The helper can also summarize, edit, and organize the work. People still have to think about who is responsible for what gets published and whether readers know how it was made.
tiers.practitioner: Applications include automated content production, data mining, news dissemination, content optimization, and AI-assisted drafting, editing, summarization, and research. Generative pre-trained transformers can generate or summarize information at scale. Implementation pitfalls include unclear transparency and accountability, effects on employment, and unresolved editorial and ethical responsibility.
tiers.paperLevel: Automated journalism comprises four main application fields: automated content production, data mining, news dissemination, and content optimization. Its scope extends beyond fully generated stories to AI-assisted newsroom workflows; central research limits and open questions concern transparency, accountability, employment, editorial responsibility, and journalistic ethics.

explainer.example: For a routine sports report, a program processes the game’s results, generates a draft article, and summarizes the key information. The same newsroom may also use AI to edit and optimize the item before dissemination.

usedIn.name: Finance reporting

usedIn.name: Sports coverage
usedIn.detail: Sports reporting can use automation for routine, data-based stories.

usedIn.name: Election coverage
usedIn.detail: Election reporting is another area where routine reporting may be automated.

usedIn.name: Newsroom workflows
usedIn.detail: AI assists with drafting, editing, summarization, research, and content optimization.

explainer.intuition: The core idea is to let software handle repeatable parts of journalism while news organizations decide how the work is checked, presented, and governed. It covers both computer-generated stories and broader assistance across the newsroom.
howItWorks: Gather information, such as data for a routine report.
Mine or process that information for material relevant to the story.
Generate, draft, edit, or summarize content with software.
Optimize the resulting content and newsroom workflow.
Disseminate the news through the organization’s publishing processes.
explainer.whyItMatters: Automation can make routine reporting more efficient and free journalists for other work. Its expanding role also makes decisions about disclosure, responsibility, employment, and editorial ethics increasingly important.
misconceptions: It does not only mean fully computer-written articles; it also includes data mining, dissemination, optimization, and assisted workflows.
Efficiency does not settle questions of transparency, accountability, or editorial responsibility.
AI-assisted journalism is broader than the idea of replacing human content creation.

diagram.caption: Automated journalism spans the path from source information to published news, including AI-assisted newsroom work.
